This documentation describes abas Java Objects - an object oriented Java API for abas ERP.

Java Object Interface

The Java object interface represents each database object as a Java object. All queries and all modifications of database objects are executed using method calls of the corresponding Java objects. In contrast to the standard FOP/EDP interfaces, there is an object-oriented view of database objects and the programmer doesn't have to think about sticking to the variable type and name, nor loading the objects in the "buffer", for example. Also no previous knowledge of the abas ERP FO programming interface is required. 

Database classes

The main components of the object-oriented database interface are the database classes; they are those classes which enable access to the database objects. In abas ERP, the database schema is described in the "Table of variables" which can be customized. Each table of variables describes a specific class of database objects, e.g. customers, products, accounts, etc. These classes are also described as "Groups" in abas ERP. A Java class, a so-called group class, for the interface is generated for each such group. It mainly contains access methods for all fields.

When editing a table of variables, the respective group class must be regenerated (using ajo_install.sh). Through new compilation of all created Java programs, you can easily determine if more changes are required.

Object model

Object models describe the objects in the system and also their relations. The object model of the abas ERP database has four hierarchy levels:
  1. Root class AbasObject: base class of all further classes
  2. Database classes: shape a specific database (also named as "file" by abas ERP) and are derived from AbasObject
  3. Group classes: shape a specific table of variables and contain getter methods for its fields; each group class is derived from their respective database class
  4. Editor classes: extend the corresponding group classes and contain setter methods for all writeable fields

About individual classes:

AbasObject: The top class of all DB objects is the interface AbasObject. It contains the implementation of a line of all database objects with common methods.

Group classes: Each selectable table of variables group has a so-called group class which inherits from its file class. There are the classes Customer, Product, etc. They mainly contain access functions for all fields.

Any method which - according to its parameter list - AbasObject, returns a database class (because at compile time the type cannot be determined more precisely), always returns an instance of a specific group class at runtime, which can then be cast to. The group classes contain methods to access the header section and the rows (presuming the table is available). Header section and rows are of the type FieldValueProvider. They contain access methods for fields.

Editor classes: Each table of variables has an editor class which may inherit from the selectable group class. There are the classes  Customer, Product, etc. They mainly contain access functions for all fields.

How do you get access to a database object?

Here are some ways you can gain access to a database object:
  1. through a database query (see Query)
  2. through a reference field of a database object already being accessed

Querys

Database queries (querys) are executed using the generic class Query. A query is parameterized with the database class (i.e. subclass of AbasObject) to which the query should be limited. If AbasObject is specified as the parameter, the whole database is searched. If one group class is specified, the search is only in this group.

Mapping of "types" of abas ERP to Java classes or primitive types

In abas ERP, with the help of a "type" of variable, the internal type is determined and the way in which this variable is output. The types defined in abas ERP are mainly abas-specific and consequentially have no immediate equivalent in Java. Therefore, it must be defined which type the get method of a variable returns with a specific type. This can be seen in the following table:

A Enum*

Some specific types are described in the following:

undefined Java type

Specific types, e.g. BU (button) can never occur as a return value of a get method, that is why the corresponding Java type is not defined (void).

Enumeration types

There is an individual class for each enumeration type in abas ERP (subclass of AbasEnum respectively). More on this in the Package documentation of de.abas.db.type.enums.

Table enumerations

A table enumeration value refers to a specific row of the enumeration data record. In the interface, it is represented by the AbasRecord interface which represents this row.

References

According to the table, all reference types are represented on a subclass of AbasObject. Here always the most exact possible subclass is used in the get and set methods because for many reference fields the exact group, or at least database, to which the reference can be made is known.

BigDecimal

REAL is mapped to double. The standard class BigDecimal may have to be used for invoice with amounts and currencies because of the rounding problem.

Package structure

The generated database classes are client-dependent. They are in the client directory. The directory name is $MANDANT/abasbase/java. Each "database" is in a package, de.abas.erp.db.schema.`file description`.

Basic classes of the database interface, e.g. the classes Query and Selection are in the de.abas.erp.db package.

Type classes are in de.abas.common.type and the classes for user-defined enumerations and the table of units in the de.abas.erp.db.schema.units or de.abas.erp.db.schema.userenum package in the client.
